source_limitations.note: Local capability evidence has carried auth, identity, telemetry, containment, and live-health limitations.
Contract/authority reconciliation is accepted with carried unknowns, not VERIFIED.
Synthesis may proceed; unknowns must remain explicit.

summary.posture: Open questions do not block independent audit of the proposed architecture. They block or constrain the named implementation, certification, execution, or promotion phases until evidence is supplied.

questions.question: Which exact authority files and tracked paths exist at the implementation commit, given that the supplied archive contains exact-name copies while the reconciliation evidence reports absent or differently located root authorities?
questions.current_architecture_default: Use runtime code, config, tests, current Git state, and tracked-path provenance. Do not treat archive filenames as proof of tracked root authority.
questions.next_evidence: Fresh git ls-files, git status, commit SHA, and content hashes for RULES, PROJECT, ARCHITECTURE, SYSTEM_BOUNDARIES, TRUTH files, and routing contracts.
questions.resolution_rule: Preserve both records until current Git evidence identifies the tracked authority and provenance.

questions.question: What is the stable, non-mutating DCP classification read interface and immutable identifier for DCPClassificationRef?
questions.current_architecture_default: Artifact-first adapter with strict schema and source hash; no DCP runtime write or authority expansion.
questions.next_evidence: Current DCP runtime entrypoint, schema, tests, and a read-only sample classification artifact at the implementation commit.
questions.resolution_rule: If no stable read interface exists, keep DCP optional and accept an operator-supplied classification ref.

questions.question: Which Freeflow API or artifact is the canonical read-only source for admission decisions, cooldowns, paid caps, estimated cost, quota buckets, and decision identifiers?
questions.current_architecture_default: Reference a normalized Freeflow decision snapshot without opening or mutating its ledger directly unless the runtime proves a supported read API.
questions.next_evidence: Freeflow runtime code, schema migrations, tests, public read methods, and sample decision records from the target commit.
questions.resolution_rule: No supported read path means Freeflow-dependent candidates remain not admitted rather than bypassed.

questions.question: Which LiteLLM proxy manager, configuration path, and trace callback are canonical when parallel LiteLLM implementations or launch surfaces coexist?
questions.current_architecture_default: Treat each observed path as a separate provider-path candidate and do not normalize them into one canonical runtime without current wiring evidence.
questions.next_evidence: Active process/compose/launch wiring, current config load path, callback registration, tests, and sample trace output.
questions.resolution_rule: Only the active entrypoint at the inspected commit may supply canonical proxy observations.

questions.question: What immutable RTE route-decision reference and schema can the Universal Router consume across the active v5 and compatibility v3/v4 surfaces?
questions.current_architecture_default: Keep RTE fully specialized and use artifact refs only; never reproduce its ladders or spend policy.
questions.next_evidence: Current RTE run manifest, phase-routing artifact, proof-pack schema, run ID semantics, and compatibility tests.
questions.resolution_rule: If cross-version identity is ambiguous, qualify refs by RTE engine version and artifact hash.

questions.question: Where is the canonical executable PR Steward runtime or command that emits MERGE_READINESS.json?
questions.current_architecture_default: Keep PRStewardReadinessRef external and require each executable task packet to locate and pin the current canonical invocation before opening a PR.
questions.next_evidence: Current runtime path, command help, schema, tests, sample output, and GitHub review-intake coverage.
questions.resolution_rule: Do not build a replacement inside the Universal Router. A missing canonical command blocks packet readiness.

questions.question: Which runner/provider paths can produce provider-controlled served-model metadata tied to a specific request and sufficient for provider_attested_model or attested_actual_model?
questions.current_architecture_default: Set attested_actual_model to UNKNOWN and cap identity confidence below ATTESTED unless explicit provider-controlled evidence is present.
questions.next_evidence: Per-provider request/response metadata, runner envelopes, proxy traces, request linkage, and adversarial identity tests.
questions.resolution_rule: Request ID alone, proxy report alone, configured model, or model-generated text is insufficient.

questions.question: Which vendors or plans expose plan-credit consumption or a provider-published token-to-credit conversion?
questions.current_architecture_default: Record plan_credits as unavailable and never derive them from tokens, cost, or elapsed time.
questions.next_evidence: Provider-published plan documentation or exact runner telemetry with measurement semantics and version.
questions.resolution_rule: Unknown credits may block a credit-hard-capped route but cannot be replaced with an estimate.

questions.question: Can the target Codex CLI version enforce all required file, command, network, MCP, environment, session, and output controls for a bounded execution adapter?
questions.current_architecture_default: Codex remains advisory only. Wrapper or OS enforcement must be independently proven before execution.
questions.next_evidence: Fresh version/help capture, safe contained probes, wrapper design, OS enforcement evidence, auth mode, session behavior, and negative escape tests.
questions.resolution_rule: Prompt instructions or an incomplete sandbox do not satisfy enforcement requirements.

questions.question: What are the authenticated Claude Code runner's actual-model, usage, cost, tool-denial, containment, and session-persistence semantics in the target environment?
questions.current_architecture_default: Use Claude Code as implementation/audit fallback only through a current approved packet; do not claim successful provider capability from the failed bare smoke.
questions.next_evidence: Contained authenticated smoke, JSON envelope, modelUsage behavior, transcript controls, tool denial, budget enforcement, and provider identity evidence.
questions.resolution_rule: An exit code of zero with an error envelope is a failed provider attempt, not success.

questions.question: Can Gemini CLI provide enforceable no-tool/no-write/no-network and no-session-persistence controls, plus reliable identity/usage telemetry?
questions.current_architecture_default: Gemini CLI is limited to broad-context advisory contradiction audits when separately approved; it is not a certified execution or independent-audit route.
questions.next_evidence: Fresh help, safe contained smoke, session/output inspection, tool/network enforcement tests, and identity/usage observations.
questions.resolution_rule: No proven containment means the candidate is ineligible for tasks requiring those controls.

questions.question: Can AGY/Sonnet satisfy the preferred embedded-auditor contract for containment, structured output, session behavior, identity, usage, cost, and safe invocation?
questions.current_architecture_default: AGY is preferred only when a current certified capability snapshot exists; otherwise use the approved Claude Code fallback and record the route.
questions.next_evidence: Exact CLI invocation, safe sandbox behavior, tool controls, structured output, log schema, identity, usage/cost, and capacity failure behavior.
questions.resolution_rule: Availability alone is insufficient; skipped AGY audit is not a pass.

questions.question: Which provider-health acquisition paths distinguish host health, proxy health, provider health, authentication, policy blocks, and sandbox/environment blocks without broad new network authority?
questions.current_architecture_default: Use explicit ProviderHealthSnapshot statuses with environment scope; no live probe is required for release-one static recommendations unless policy requires freshness.
questions.next_evidence: Approved health endpoints, probe wrappers, response classifications, rate/cost behavior, and sandbox-versus-host comparison.
questions.resolution_rule: Sandbox denial cannot mark provider or host unavailable.

questions.question: Are the proposed TTLs for versions, containment, authentication, provider health, environment failures, vendor catalogs, and benchmark certifications appropriate for actual operations?
questions.current_architecture_default: Use visible policy defaults: version/help 7 days, containment 7 days, auth 15 minutes, positive health 5 minutes, transient environment failure 60 seconds, vendor catalog 24 hours, benchmark certification at most 30 days.
questions.next_evidence: Shadow-mode staleness defects, provider change frequency, auth expiry behavior, and operator refresh burden.
questions.resolution_rule: Policy may shorten TTLs freely; lengthening a hard-safety TTL requires recertification.

questions.question: What are the approved retention, encryption, backup, access, and redaction requirements for router journals, task text, snapshot artifacts, and evaluation corpora?
questions.current_architecture_default: Store hashes and external refs where possible, redact before storage, use workspace-local access, and apply conservative retention subject to repository governance.
questions.next_evidence: Repository/org data policy, client obligations, threat model review, backup policy, and operator requirements.
questions.resolution_rule: Sensitive raw content is not retained until an explicit policy authorizes it.

questions.question: Are Git history, reviewed active-pointer changes, and content hashes sufficient for executable-policy integrity, or are detached signatures required?
questions.current_architecture_default: Use tracked immutable policy files, content hashes, reviewed promotion, and append-only activation records. Treat signatures as an optional future control.
questions.next_evidence: Threat/risk decision, deployment trust boundary, CI signing capability, and governance requirement.
questions.resolution_rule: If signatures become required, unsigned policies remain readable history but cannot be activated.

questions.question: How many historical tasks can be legally and reliably labeled for the initial 200-task certification corpus?
questions.current_architecture_default: Do not lower safety thresholds to fit corpus scarcity; begin with schema/hard-negative tests and collect shadow data until class coverage is sufficient.
questions.next_evidence: Inventory of task packets, PRs, investigations, proof bundles, privacy constraints, duplicates, and reviewer availability.
questions.resolution_rule: Unresolved or duplicate tasks do not count toward certification minima.

questions.question: Which external system issues, stores, expires, and verifies HumanApprovalRef records?
questions.current_architecture_default: The router accepts only a validated external ref with scope, reason, approver, issue time, expiry, and evidence hash; it does not own approval state.
questions.next_evidence: Current operator/governance approval workflow, schema, identity source, revocation behavior, and sample records.
questions.resolution_rule: No valid external ref means the approval-required transition remains blocked.

questions.question: Should Codex be the first execution adapter after release-one certification?
questions.current_architecture_default: Codex is the leading candidate, not an accepted decision, because it has the strongest contained local probe among supplied runners.
questions.next_evidence: Fresh comparative capability, containment, identity, telemetry, cost/credits, reliability, and operator-fit certification for all candidate runners.
questions.resolution_rule: Select one adapter by current evidence and reversibility, not vendor preference.

questions.question: What exact adapter/version identifiers and compatibility guarantees exist for proof, handoff, audit, dopetask, and PR Steward references?
questions.current_architecture_default: Require source schema version, adapter version, content hash, and explicit unsupported-version failure for every ref adapter.
questions.next_evidence: Canonical schemas, migration rules, adapter contracts, sample bundles, and backward-compatibility tests at the implementation commit.
questions.resolution_rule: Unknown versions are not coerced; dependent claims remain blocked or unavailable.
